context: Four older adults gather for a community event. Three widowed women plus retired Hiroshi-boss.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 皆さん、お久しぶり。お元気そうで、安心しました。
lines.en: Everyone, it's been quite a while. I'm relieved to see you all looking so well.
lines.style: Warm greeting with composed authority. Steady opening. Soft but clear. The genuine pleasure of an elder reconnecting—not effusive, but unmistakably sincere. Measured pace throughout.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 田中さん、お元気そうで、何より。
lines.en: Tanaka-san, I'm so glad you're looking well.
lines.style: Gentle reciprocal warmth. A grandmother's voice—soft and sure. Brief pause before his name, like seeing an old friend. Tender closing tilt. Real pleasure, no performance.

lines.speaker: mrs_mori_neighbor
lines.jp: 皆さんで、こうやって、揃えるって、本当に、貴重ですね。
lines.en: For all of us to gather like this—it's truly precious.
lines.style: Warm reflective wonder. Slight breathiness on 'gather.' Slower pace, letting the moment settle. A neighbor noticing something beautiful and wanting everyone to notice it too. Trailing softness at the end.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: お互い、年取って、こうやって、お友達でいられるって、ありがたい。
lines.en: To get older together and still be friends like this—truly something to be grateful for.
lines.style: Deep, philosophical warmth. A gentle aunt offering perspective. Steady, unhurried delivery. Weight on 'grateful.' Not wistful—grounded. The voice of someone who has learned what matters.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 退職してから、こんな、ご縁、ありがたい。
lines.en: After retirement, to have a bond like this—I'm grateful for it.
lines.style: Measured and sincere. A boss transformed by time away. Softer than his greeting, but still composed. Slight pause before 'grateful'—acknowledgment of the shift life has brought him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 主人も、絶対、見てくれてる。
lines.en: My husband—I'm sure he's watching over this.
lines.style: Tender certainty. A grandmother's faith. Quiet and steady, not wavering. Soft gaze outward. Brief but carries weight. The voice of someone speaking to both the living and the remembered.

lines.speaker: mrs_mori_neighbor
lines.jp: うちも、同じ気持ち。本当に。
lines.style: Warm, matching assent. A neighbor stepping in to echo what matters. Simple and direct. Soft emphasis on 'truly'—the word confirms what she feels. Small, genuine.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 皆で、ね。家族みたいに、ずっと、繋がっていきたい。
lines.en: All of us together. Like family—I want us to stay connected like this.
lines.style: Warm hope extending forward. An aunt's generosity of heart. Building slightly toward 'stay connected'—not urgency, but emphasis on what matters. Gentle resolve at the close.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: こうやって、人生、繋がっていくの、本当に、幸せ。
lines.en: Life connects like this—it's truly what makes us happy.
lines.style: Composed philosophical warmth. A boss finding his deeper voice. Slow, deliberate pace. The words come from reflection, not performance. Soft trailing close—contentment settling in.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: こんな時間、本当に、ありがたい。
lines.en: Moments like this—I'm truly grateful for them.
lines.style: Brief, tender gratitude. A grandmother's simple truth. Quiet and direct. Slight pause before 'grateful'—the word carries her recognition of something precious. Soft, brief close.

lines.speaker: mrs_mori_neighbor
lines.jp: これからも、ずっと、皆さんで。
lines.en: From now on too—all of us together.
lines.style: Warm forward glance. A neighbor's gentle promise. Steady, unhurried. 'From now on' carries quiet hope. Close with a soft, extending warmth—looking ahead but rooted in the present.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.en: I'm truly grateful—for all of this.
lines.style: Sincere closing warmth. An aunt's simple, deep thanks. Quiet strength underneath. Brief pause before 'grateful'—letting the word land. Soft trailing close with genuine emotion.
